## The critical path

```{mermaid}
flowchart TB
  C["Model credentials"] --> E
  R["Record the library"] --> E
  E["make eval CONFIG=fb-v1 SPLIT=test_id"] --> S["make site-stats"]
  E --> G["Cost table, cascade comparison, judge calibration, GEPA, ablation A6"]
  style C fill:#fff8e8
  style R fill:#fff8e8
```

Nothing on the right can move until both boxes on the left are done, and neither is an
engineering task.

## In order

### 1. Model credentials

Any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, Ollama included:

```bash
export LLM_BASE_URL=http://localhost:11434/v1
export LLM_API_KEY=ollama
```

Unblocks, in one step: the cost per investigation, the cascade comparison, the judge's
calibration against human labels, prompt optimisation, ablation A6, and replay cassettes that
record a real investigation rather than a deterministic stub's imitation of one.

Without credentials the graph's deterministic floor publishes triage's answer with a label saying
no AI analysis happened. That label is the signal, and it is on every report in the repository
today.

### 2. Record the library

```bash
caffeinate -dims make lab-record-library
```

About thirty hours of wall clock remain. It cannot be compressed: each scenario's baseline,
incident and recovery have to actually happen. The recorder is resumable and decides what to
skip from the bundles on disk rather than from its own progress file, because a progress file can
be stale and a bundle either exists or does not.

::: {.callout-important}
## On mains power

Six of the first fourteen recordings were corrupted by a laptop sleeping mid-run. The monotonic
clock stops while the wall clock jumps, so the bundle looks complete and has a hole in the
middle of it. The recorder now refuses such a bundle, but the cheaper fix is a cable.
:::

Record in split order. A partly recorded library is still useful if the recorded part is a whole
split rather than a scattering.

### 3. Then the numbers appear by themselves

```bash
make eval CONFIG=b0    SPLIT=test_id   # the floor first
make eval CONFIG=fb-v1 SPLIT=test_id
make eval CONFIG=fb-v1 SPLIT=test_ood  # did it generalise or memorise
make site-stats
```

`make site-stats` regenerates every number the README and both sites publish. No template is
edited: the pages are built so that a stated absence becomes a stated figure the moment its
report says `quotable_as_a_result`.

## Open questions that need a decision, not code

| Question | Why it is not mine to make |
|---|---|
| Where the recorded library is hosted | It is roughly 870 MB and git-ignored, so `v1.0.0` ships without it |
| Whether the Console may read a reviewer's answer | `firebreak.web` is an agent package and feedback holds a true root cause |
| `PYSEC-2026-2447` in `diskcache`, which has no fix | Carried explicitly in the threat model rather than suppressed; releasing makes it a published decision |
| **Should the exit gate get a seventh check, for whether a claim is informative?** | It would fail every showcase report today. That is either the right answer or a reason to wait for a model |
| Is `reports/feedback` ground truth for the leakage rules? | It holds a human's statement of what broke, which for a held-out incident is the label |
| Correct or keep `recording_progress.json`, which overstates by three | Correcting it erases the only record of the corruption incident |

## The two problems worth solving next

Neither is blocked on credentials or recordings. Both are recorded with the evidence behind them.

::: {.panel-tabset}
### Latency faults need a second signal

The abstention rule misses the two latency faults in the recorded set because they score *below*
the healthy recording on top anomaly z. No threshold on that one statistic can separate them.

What it needs: a latency-specific signal, probably a distributional shift in the p99 rather than
a z-score on the mean. That is a measurement problem with a clear shape, and it is the single
change most likely to move the abstention figure.

### The ranking blames the symptom

It names `frontend` for all three payment failures on the recorded set. Personalised PageRank
over the service graph was supposed to prevent exactly that.

The ablation numbers say endpoint scaling carries most of the benefit and onset ordering
contributes nothing measurable *on fixtures*, where accuracy is saturated at 100% and there is no
room to demonstrate anything. On recordings there is room. Re-running that ablation on real
recordings is the first thing to do after the library exists.
:::

## What this project already demonstrates

Even unmeasured, and stated plainly rather than as a claim about performance:

- An evaluation harness that **reports honestly when it has nothing to report**, and a build that
  refuses to publish a figure its own report marks unquotable.
- Ground-truth leakage made mechanically impossible rather than carefully avoided, with an
  import-graph walk that has caught two real routes.
- A system that **abstains**, states the threshold it failed, and lets a reader disagree with it.
- Fourteen decision records that include the measurements which contradicted published
  technique, and the changes that were refused despite looking good.

The thing it does not demonstrate is that it finds root causes. That needs the two inputs above,
and until then every page says so.
